thread.title: Cryptocurrencies: The Most Pro-Islamic Payment Method Or Haram?

author: OlympTrade
title: Cryptocurrencies: The Most Pro-Islamic Payment Method Or Haram?
text:
OlympTrade Articles (9) Our Website
On January 3, 2018, the Egyptian Grand Mufti Sheikh Shawki Allam issued an official fatwa, banning bitcoin. According to the highest official of religious law, cryptocurrency isn’t an acceptable interface of exchange, and it could potentially undermine the Egyptian economy.
A real storm of discussions followed Shawki Allam’s statement, but Islamic experts avoided voicing harsh assessments. Scientists and theologians have not come to a common opinion regarding cryptocurrency yet. This issue is still being discussed.
Islamic finance experts, such as Prof Dr Ziyaad Mahomed, Associate Dean of e-learning at INCEIF, The Global University of Islamic Finance, express a more democratic position on bitcoin, drawing analogies to the appearance of paper money in the economy.
Ziyaad Mahomed, referring to the norms of sharia, states that public acceptance is necessary for the recognition of something as currency. In fact, if Muslims agree to use cryptocurrency as money, it will become money.
What does Islam say about money?
According to Sharia, a resource that is easy to get cannot be money. An economic collapse may occur if everyone has access to the means of payment. This is the reason why Muslim’s opinions diverged.
On the one hand, we understand that everyone can become a miner. However, this process will not bring a cent without buying the equipment. Mining using the proof-of-work function implies a certain material and technical base, which is indirectly taken into account by the market when forming the current market value of a digital coin.
And making money by proof of stake kind of mining has signs of riba (the charging of interest). However, this question cannot be unambiguously answered, since in that case a miner is a guarantor of the means of payment, and not the usurer.
Sharia law provides for a mandatory confirmation of money availability. Any cryptocurrency is primarily a computer code. All information about the transactions carried out within the network of a particular cryptocurrency is recorded. People can see not only the number of coins in their wallet, but also the availability of funds of their counterparties, if they know their ID.
But various ICO projects may fail to comply with sharia regulations due to a weak level of security, as well as unclear prospects. Many of them do have features of financial pyramids that promise hundreds percent of profit.
Money and maysir
The high volatility of cryptocurrencies is, perhaps, the most critical moment of the use of digital money by Muslims. According to some religious leaders, large swings in value have features of maysir.
But what should one think of the Turkish lira, which has weakened by half against a US dollar? Volatility is a normal feature of modern actively developing products. For example, during 2018, Apple shares (NASDAQ: AAPL ) rose by 25%, and Visa (NYSE: V ) - by 29%.
There are cryptocurrencies with a high degree of reliability, which has been proven by several years of successful operation. One can use these coins to pay for a product or service. The number of enterprises that accept these assets as a means of payment increases every day.
Cryptocurrencies and the state
Until recently, currency issuance was entirely concentrated in the hands of governments. Only central banks could infuse money into the economy.
Some experts consider the lack of communication between the state and cryptocurrencies to be unacceptable for Muslims. At the same time, the issued amount of popular cryptocurrencies, such as bitcoin, litecoin, etc. is limited by the source code.
Due to this specificity, these assets are not subject to either inflation or the influence of central banks’ interest rates. And this complies best with the Islamic law, that prohibits the bank interest.
Some segments of the crypto market have already begun to form ties with the state. The example of the Dubai government that created emCash cryptocurrency has already influenced other countries, and Japanese and American citizens are already paying taxes on income made from cryptocurrencies. South Korea, Russia and many other countries are actively engaged in this area.
To sum up
It is impossible to characterize the entire digital money market in terms of sharia unambiguously. However, leading cryptocurrencies not only do not contradict the basics of religious norms, but also prove to be even more suitable for a Muslim than the classical fiat currency.
